quarterly_data.signal: CEO Albert Bourla: Pfizer's new products and business-development products are running at around a $13 billion annualized rate and growing in the 20s percent, the basis for offsetting the coming LOEs; Pfizer beat revenue expectations in nine of its last 10 earnings reports and EPS in 10 out of 10. The HHS 340B pilot starting in January 2027 covers two significant Pfizer products, ELIQUIS and IBRANCE (a pilot Pfizer 'worked very hard to make sure that happens'); he would not count on a major 340B benefit, as the recent effect was net marginally positive.
quarterly_data.figure: around $13 billion annualized rate for new and business-development products

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Albert Bourla on obesity: Pfizer is running 20 obesity studies this year, 10 of them Phase III in the Metsera portfolio; the weekly (diabetes and non-diabetes) and monthly Phase III studies have started and 'pretty much' fully recruited in record time; the SWITCH study (people plateaued on other GLP-1s moving to monthly maintenance, designed for non-inferiority) starts this year. The Phase III program adds a titration step (to twice the dose before four times) and allows patients to step down a dose after a tolerability issue, which earlier Metsera studies did not; he expects a monthly product with very good tolerability and the efficacy of weekly GLP-1s. The monthly amylin plus GLP-1 combination Phase II has started and reads out next year, Phase I data come toward the end of this year, and the final Phase III starts next year. A licensed oral GLP-1 on the same scaffold as orforglipron but needing a much smaller dose (so it can be combined in a pill) is 'quite advanced'.
quarterly_data.figure: 20 obesity studies this year, 10 Phase III

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Albert Bourla: Pfizer owns mevrometostat 100% globally (versus sharing XTANDI); the Phase III readout is delayed only because there are fewer events than anticipated, and Pfizer estimates it will know before the end of the year; the earlier randomized data showed a 50% improvement, and even a 30% improvement would be very meaningful and statistically significant. Business development will be strategic and careful, with 'a lot in China' at earlier stages (peri-IND, Phase I, Phase II); Pfizer has 1,500 R&D people in China and sends teams on the ground for patient-level due diligence; he expects global Chinese pharma players by the end of the decade and sees AI as the biggest lever to reach 'half the cost and three times the speed'.
quarterly_data.figure: 50% improvement in earlier randomized data; 1,500 R&D people in China
